studies.title: The Mongol post
studies.caption: Ögedei Khan sets up relay stations a day's ride apart across the empire, with fresh horses and food for anyone carrying the khan's pass, the paiza.
studies.prompt: Eye-level inside a thirteenth-century Mongol relay station: foreground hands inspect a plain rectangular metal paiza with a suspension hole and small indistinct vertical marks, while a messenger in belted deel and cap waits. Fresh horses and low felt tents visible through doorway. Focus pass and practical hospitality, unlike the wide Persian horse-change scene. No readable invented script, no modern passport, no monumental palace.
